subject: Anthropology
title: The Indus Valley Civilization
description: A fast breakdown of The Indus Valley Civilization for builders.

hook.text: Mohenjo-daro had flush toilets, covered drains, and a grid street plan — in 2500 BCE. Then it vanished.

buildup.text: The Indus Valley civilization spanned modern Pakistan and India with planned cities and standardized weights.

discovery.text: There are no palaces, no royal tombs, and no obvious kings. Its power structure remains an archaeological mystery.

twist.text: Its script has never been deciphered. Without reading their writing, we can't fully understand their world.

climax.text: The Indus Valley challenges assumptions. A complex civilization existed without obvious monarchy or military display.

punchline.text: A civilization that ran on order, not kings.

quiz.question: What is unusual about the Indus Valley civilization?
options: It had the largest army in history
It shows no clear evidence of kings or palaces

details.summary: The Indus Valley Civilization (3300-1300 BCE) was one of the world's earliest urban societies, spanning modern Pakistan and northwest India. Its planned cities, standardized weights, sophisticated drainage systems, and undeciphered script remain among archaeology's greatest puzzles.
details.whyItMatters: The Indus Civilization challenges assumptions about early states. It shows remarkably little evidence of warfare, palaces, or rulers — suggesting that complex urban societies can organize without obvious centralized authority or violent coercion.
takeaways: The Indus Civilization featured planned cities and standardized systems
Its script remains undeciphered despite extensive study
It challenges assumptions about the necessity of centralized authority

faq.question: Why has the Indus script not been deciphered?
faq.answer: The inscriptions are very short — averaging just five symbols. There is no bilingual inscription like the Rosetta Stone. The underlying language is unknown, and some scholars question whether the symbols represent full writing rather than a symbol system.

faq.question: How did the Indus Civilization collapse?
faq.answer: Climate change, shifting river courses, earthquakes, and possible epidemic disease are all proposed factors. The collapse was gradual rather than sudden. Urban populations dispersed to smaller settlements, and the distinctive material culture slowly faded over centuries.
